what_it_is.prose: The AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft) is India's programme to develop a fifth-generation, twin-engine, stealth-capable medium fighter — the most ambitious indigenous combat-aircraft project ever attempted by India. Designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA, a DRDO body) and to be produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), the AMCA is intended to give the Indian Air Force and Navy a modern stealth fighter that competes with the F-35, Su-57 and J-20 in the medium class, with full Indian design ownership of the airframe, stealth shaping, avionics, sensor fusion and weapons integration. The programme has progressed through concept and detailed design under an approved development budget; the first flight was originally targeted around the mid-2030s but has been delayed from earlier estimates (the programme has slipped). The AMCA will use two GE F414 engines in its initial Mk-1 configuration, stepping to a more powerful engine (a newer/more-powerful engine under consideration) on the later Mk-2. It will carry an internal weapons bay for stealth strike, the indigenous Uttam AESA radar, and Indian air-to-air and strike weapons including Astra and, on later variants, BrahMos-NG-class or SLCM air-launched systems. Strategically, AMCA is the end-point of India's decades-long attempt to achieve genuine fifth-generation combat-aircraft sovereignty — the capability to design, iterate and sustain a modern stealth fighter without dependence on any foreign OEM. It is a direct counterpart to China's J-20 programme and a hedge against reliance on Russian Su-57 or US F-35 imports. Its success or failure will define whether India's military-aerospace industrial base can stand alone at the frontier of the technology.

deployments_procurement.summary: The AMCA remains in the development phase; funding was approved and detailed design is under way at ADA/HAL. No production order exists yet. The IAF has stated intent to order a sizeable fleet once the aircraft matures. First flight has slipped from earlier estimates to the 2030s timeframe (~2032-35).

faq.question: What makes the AMCA fifth-generation?
faq.answer: The AMCA is fifth-generation because of its stealth shaping, internal weapons bays, reduced radar cross-section, integrated sensor fusion and the Uttam AESA radar — capabilities that put it in the class of the F-35, Su-57 and J-20 rather than a conventional fourth-generation fighter.

faq.question: Who is designing the AMCA?
faq.answer: The AMCA is designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA, a DRDO body), which designed the Tejas, and will be produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). The Indian Air Force and Navy are potential customers.

faq.question: What engine will the AMCA use?
faq.answer: The initial Mk-1 AMCA will use two GE F414 engines (imported/licensed). A later Mk-2 is planned to use a more powerful engine, the choice and indigenisation path of which is still under consideration — the engine is the programme's single largest dependence.

faq.question: When will the AMCA fly?
faq.answer: First flight has repeatedly slipped; it is now targeted around the 2030s (~2032-35). Production and induction would follow several years later. The programme remains in detailed design.
